answer: One defence is requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake tied to a single verified hardware key before it can transact. A lightweight raven node can open a channel with a tiny stake, but a sparrow-scale fleet of fake identities must fund every identity separately, so the cost of a Sybil swarm grows linearly with its size. Honest agents that behave well earn their stake back with interest, while detected fakes lose theirs, and the ripple of each confiscation is published on the ledger so other agents can price the risk of dealing with unproven newcomers.
